polls.description: China's AI companies are experiencing explosive growth and competition while facing geopolitical tensions with the US and EU over technology access.
polls.question: Will US tech restrictions ultimately strengthen or weaken China's AI sector?

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia Says Company Firing Up H200 Production for China
cluster_stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the company has been licensed for “many customers in China” for H200 sales and is in the process of “restarting our manufacturing.” Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA FIRES UP H200 Production for China - Huang Confirms

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia is restarting production of China AI chip variant, says CEO Jensen Huang
cluster_stories.summary: Nvidia is restarting ⁠the production of one of the company’s chips that is designed to comply with US export restrictions on China, CEO Jensen Huang said at a press conference on Tuesday. The company had halted ‌manufacturing last year of its H200 chip, which is based on its ageing Hopper technology, because of increasing regulatory hurdles in the US and China, according to a report at the time. cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA RESTARTS China AI Chip Production Despite Export Bans

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia nears AI chip exports to China after US approval delays
cluster_stories.summary: Chief executive Jensen Huang says company received flood of orders and American licences over past two weeks
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA NEARS AI CHIP EXPORTS TO CHINA AFTER US APPROVAL

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Says Company Is Firing Up H200 Production for China
cluster_stories.summary: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said the company is firing up manufacturing of H200 AI accelerators for customers in China, a sign of progress in the chipmaker’s effort to reenter the vital market.
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA CEO: Firing Up H200 Production for China

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia Forecasts $1 Trillion in Revenue Through 2027 | Bloomberg Tech 3/17/2026
cluster_stories.summary: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss Nvidia's prediction that it will generate $1 trillion in sales through 2027. Plus, IBM CEO Arvind Krishna talks about the AI and M&A landscape, hot off the company's own GTC announcement. And, the CEO of Gecko Robotics explains how the startup deploys its AI-powered robots to assess the condition and readiness of the US Navy's warships. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA FORECASTS $1 TRILLION REVENUE BY 2027

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia eyes $1 trillion in revenue through 2027: What's driving this growth?
cluster_stories.summary: This signals Huang's confidence that Nvidia will remain the biggest company in the market for AI chips even as competition grows. Investors have also doubted whether its strategy of plowing ‌back its profits ⁠into the ⁠AI ecosystem is paying off.
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA EYES $1 TRILLION REVENUE BY 2027

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Huang Expects to Make $1 Trillion From AI Chips
cluster_stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the company expects to generate at least $1 trillion from its Blackwell and Rubin chips through the end of 2027. He speaks during Nvidia's GTC event in San Jose, California. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA CEO CLAIMS $1 TRILLION CHIP REVENUE BY 2027
